entries.title: The Question Worth Asking
entries.originalScriptText:
तपःस्वाध्यायनिरतं तपस्वी वाग्विदां वरम् |
नारदं परिपप्रच्छ वाल्मीकिर्मुनिपुङ्गवम् || १||
को न्वस्मिन्साम्प्रतं लोके गुणवान्कश्च वीर्यवान् |
धर्मज्ञश्च कृतज्ञश्च सत्यवाक्यो दृढव्रतः || २||
चारित्रेण च को युक्तः सर्वभूतेषु को हितः |
विद्वान्कः कः समर्थश्च कश्चैकप्रियदर्शनः || ३||
आत्मवान्को जितक्रोधो मतिमान्कोऽनसूयकः |
कस्य बिभ्यति देवाश्च जातरोषस्य संयुगे || ४||
एतदिच्छाम्यहं श्रोतुं परं कौतूहलं हि मे |
महर्षे त्वं समर्थोऽसि ज्ञातुमेवंविधं नरम् || ५||
entries.transliteration:
tapaḥsvādhyāyanirataṃ tapasvī vāgvidāṃ varam | nāradaṃ paripapraccha vālmīkirmunipuṅgavam || 1 ||
ko nvasminsāmprataṃ loke guṇavānkaśca vīryavān | dharmajñaśca kṛtajñaśca satyavākyo dṛḍhavrataḥ || 2 ||
cāritreṇa ca ko yuktaḥ sarvabhūteṣu ko hitaḥ | vidvānkaḥ kaḥ samarthaśca kaścaikapriyadarśanaḥ || 3 ||
ātmavānko jitakrodho matimānko'nasūyakaḥ | kasya bibhyati devāśca jātaroṣasya saṃyuge || 4 ||
etadicchāmyahaṃ śrotuṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me | maharṣe tvaṃ samartho'si jñātumevaṃvidhaṃ naram || 5 ||

translationEn.text:
To sainted Nárad, prince of those
Whose lore in words of wisdom flows.
Whose constant care and chief delight
Were Scripture and ascetic rite,
The good Válmíki, first and best
Of hermit saints, these words addressed:
“In all this world, I pray thee, who
Is virtuous, heroic, true?
Firm in his vows, of grateful mind,
To every creature good and kind?
Bounteous, and holy, just, and wise,
Alone most fair to all men’s eyes?
Devoid of envy, firm, and sage,
Whose tranquil soul ne’er yields to rage?
Whom, when his warrior wrath is high,
Do Gods embattled fear and fly?
Whose noble might and gentle skill
The triple world can guard from ill?
Who is the best of princes, he
Who loves his people’s good to see?
The store of bliss, the living mine
Where brightest joys and virtues shine?
Queen Fortune’s best and dearest friend,
Whose steps her choicest gifts attend?
Who may with Sun and Moon compare,
With Indra, Vishṇu, Fire, and Air?
Grant, Saint divine, the boon I ask,
For thee, I ween, an easy task,
To whom the power is given to know
If such a man breathe here below.”

entries.explanation: The epic opens with a question, not a battle. The sage Valmiki asks the divine sage Narada to name a person who is truly virtuous, capable, grateful, truthful, steady in his vows, kind to all beings and free of envy and anger. Narada's reply, which follows in the same sarga, introduces Rama.
entries.lifeApplication: Before judging anyone by success or power, it helps to ask what qualities we actually admire: honesty, gratitude, self-control, care for others. Naming them clearly makes them easier to practise.
entries.reflectionPrompt: Which one quality from this list would you most like to grow in yourself this week, and what is one small action that practises it?
